example: The memoranda were filed by date.
note: 纯屈折形式
derivation: memor（记忆；留心） + anda（名词后缀（动形词）） → 备忘录（复数）

example: She circulated a memorandum on costs.
etymology: 拉丁 memorandum「应被记住之事」
derivation: memor（记忆；留心） + and（名词后缀（动形词）） + um（名词后缀（单数）） → 备忘录

example: Three memorandums arrived this morning.
note: 屈折形式：英语化复数 -s
derivation: memor（记忆；留心） + and（名词后缀（动形词）） + um（名词后缀（单数）） → 备忘录（英语化复数）
menstru（每月的） + al（形容词后缀） → menstrual
example: The app tracks the menstrual cycle.

glossEn: the chemical processes that sustain life
etymology: 希腊 metabolē「改变」< meta-（转变）+ ballein（投掷）
derivation: meta（转变）+ bol（投）+ -ism → 体内不断转换的过程
example: Regular exercise raises your resting metabolism.

glossEn: changed in form, especially rock altered by heat
etymology: 希腊 meta-（转变）+ morphē「形状」+ -ic
derivation: meta（转变）+ morph（形状）+ -ic → 形状改变的
example: Marble is a metamorphic rock derived from limestone.

glossEn: a figure of speech applying one thing's name to another
etymology: 希腊 metaphora「转移」< meta-（越过）+ pherein（携带）
derivation: meta（越过）+ phor（携带）→ 把意义搬过去
example: 'A sea of troubles' is a metaphor.

glossEn: relating to measurement; based on the metre
derivation: metr（度量）+ -ic → 关于度量的
example: The lab reports every figure in metric units.

glossEn: a small chip that runs a computer
derivation: micro（微小） + process（进程） + or（施动者） → microprocessor
example: The board carries a 32-bit microprocessor.

derivation: micro（微小） + scopy（观察术） → microscopy
example: Electron microscopy revealed the pores.

derivation: micro（微小） + second（秒） → microsecond
example: The switch reacts in a microsecond.

derivation: micro（微小） + struct（建造） + ure（名词后缀） → microstructure
example: Etching revealed the alloy's microstructure.
The country doubled military spending.
etymology: 拉丁 militaris < miles 士兵
derivation: milit（士兵；战斗） + ary（形容词/名词后缀） → 军事的

etymology: 拉丁 mille「千」+ 法语 gramme「克」
derivation: milli（千分之一）+ gram（克）→ 千分之一克
example: The tablet contains five milligrams of the drug.

derivation: milli（千分之一）+ metr（米）+ -er → 千分之一米
example: The crack widened by a millimeter each year.
He played a minor role in the film.
etymology: 拉丁 minor < minus 更少
derivation: min（小；少） + or（名词后缀：施动者（拉丁来源）） → 较小的；未成年人
mis（错误地） + align（对齐） → misalign
example: One gear can misalign the whole train.

glossEn: unacceptable behaviour by someone in a position of trust
derivation: mis-（错误地）+ conduct（行为、引导）→ 错误的行为
example: The report documents repeated misconduct by the contractor.

derivation: mis（错误） + in（向内/不） + form（形状；形成） + ation（名词后缀） → misinformation
example: Misinformation spread faster than the correction.

derivation: mis（错误地） + take（拿） → mistake
example: That was a costly mistake.

derivation: mob（移动） + ile（形容词后缀） → mobile
example: The clinic runs a mobile screening unit.

ety.from: 法语 modèle，源自意大利 modello，最终来自拉丁 modulus（小量度，modus 的指小形式）
ety.note: 本义是“小量度、标准尺寸”，经法语进入英语后指“样板、模范”，再隐喻扩展为“模型、模式”；现代机器学习中的“模型”是这一隐喻链的最新一环。

derivation: modern（现代的） + ise（动词后缀） → modernise
example: The port plans to modernise its cranes.

derivation: modern（现代的） + ity（名词后缀） → modernity
example: The building mixes tradition with modernity.

derivation: modern（现代的） + ize（动词后缀） → modernize
example: They will modernize the heating system.

glossEn: the smallest unit of a compound
example: A water molecule has three atoms.
etymology: 拉丁 molecula，moles 块体的指小
derivation: mole（团块；质量） + cule（指小后缀） → 分子

example: The campaign gained momentum in June.
derivation: mo（移动） + ment（名词后缀：行为、结果、手段） + um（名词后缀（单数）） → 动量；势头

glossEn: the practice of having one spouse at a time
etymology: 希腊 monos「单一」+ gamos「婚姻」
derivation: mono（一）+ gam（婚配）+ -y → 只结一次婚
example: Monogamy is the legal norm in most of the country.

derivation: mono（单一） + lingu（舌头、语言） + al（形容词后缀） → monolingual
example: The dictionary is aimed at monolingual learners.

glossEn: a large single block of stone
derivation: mono（单一）+ lith（石）→ 一整块石头
example: A weathered monolith stands at the centre of the ring.

glossEn: a long speech by one person
derivation: mono（单一） + logue（言、说） → monologue
example: The actor opened with a two-minute monologue.

derivation: mono（单一） + poly（卖，希腊 polein） → monopoly
example: The firm held a monopoly on parts for years.
note: poly 在此为希腊 polein“卖”，与 poly-“多”同形异源

example: A monument marks the old gate.
etymology: 拉丁 monumentum < monere 提醒
note: mon- 与 mono-（单一）同形，解析歧义，故不标 verified
derivation: mon（提醒） + ument（……手段/结果（名）） → 纪念碑

glossEn: the study of form and structure
derivation: morph（形状）+ o + logy（学科）→ 研究形态的学问
example: The course covers the morphology of flowering plants.
The body was taken to the mortuary.
derivation: mort（死） + uary（……的场所（名）） → 太平间

ety.from: motor + hotel 的混成词
ety.note: 20 世纪 20 年代美国公路旅行的产物，取 motor 的首部与 hotel 的尾部。

derivation: multi（多） + core（核心） → multicore
example: The laptop uses a multicore chip.

derivation: multi（多） + form（形状；形成） → multiform
example: The disease is multiform and hard to classify.

glossEn: involving three or more parties or countries
derivation: mult（多）+ i + later（边）+ -al → 多边的
example: The two sides signed a multilateral trade agreement.

derivation: multi（多） + lingu（舌头、语言） + al（形容词后缀） → multilingual
example: The staff are multilingual and patient.

derivation: multi（多） + media（媒介） → multimedia
example: The exhibit uses multimedia throughout.

glossEn: consisting of more than one part or instance
etymology: 拉丁 multiplex < multus「多」+ plicare（折叠）
derivation: mult（多）+ i + ple（折）→ 折成多层 → 多个的
example: The report lists multiple causes for the failure.

ety.from: 拉丁 musculus（小老鼠，mus 的指小形式）
ety.note: 因肌肉收缩时形似小老鼠而得名；现代义与“老鼠”已无共时联系。

etymology: nano-（希腊 nanos 侏儒，引申十亿分之一）+ metre（希腊 metron 尺）
derivation: nano（十亿分之一）+ metre（米）→ nanometre；英式拼写 -re，美式作 nanometer
example: The coating is only a few nanometres thick.

etymology: nano-（纳米）+ structure，20 世纪晚期
derivation: nano（纳米） + struct（建造） + ure（名词后缀） → nanostructure
example: The coating forms a regular nanostructure.

glossEn: engineering of materials at the nanometre scale
etymology: nano-（纳米级）+ 希腊 tekhnē（技艺）+ -logia（学科）
derivation: nano（纳米级）+ techn（技艺）+ o（连接元音）+ logy（学科）→ nanotechnology
example: Nanotechnology may shrink the sensor to a grain of dust.

ety.from: National Aeronautics and Space Administration 的首字母缩略词
ety.note: 1958 年成立，按字母组合读作一个词（acronym），不是词素组合。

example: The nation held a general election.
etymology: 拉丁 natio < nasci 出生
derivation: nat（出生；来源） + ion（名词后缀（-tion 家族的词干形式）） → 国家；民族

example: She is a native speaker of Thai.
etymology: 拉丁 nativus < nasci 出生
derivation: nat（出生；来源） + ive（形容词后缀：具有……性质的） → 本地的；天生的

glossEn: existing in nature, not made by people
etymology: 拉丁 naturalis < natura（天性）< nasci（出生）
derivation: natur（出生、天性）+ al（形容词后缀）→ natural
example: The cave keeps a natural temperature all year.

glossEn: to plan and direct a course, especially at sea
etymology: 拉丁 navigare < navis「船」+ agere（驱动）
derivation: nav（船）+ -ig-（驱动）+ -ate → 驾船前行
example: They navigated the channel without a pilot.

glossEn: a country's military force at sea
etymology: 古法语 navie「船队」< 拉丁 navis「船」
derivation: nav（船）+ -y（集合）→ 船队 → 海军
example: He served in the navy for six years.
The test gave a negative result.
etymology: 拉丁 negativus < negare 否认
derivation: neg（否定） + ative（形容词后缀：具有……作用的） → 否定的；消极的

ety.from: net + citizen 的混成词
ety.note: 20 世纪 90 年代互联网文化用语，取 net 与 citizen 的尾部拼合。

ety.from: net（网）+ work（劳作、制品）的复合词
ety.note: 19 世纪先指铁路网、电报网等“像网一样连成的系统”，20 世纪下半叶扩展为计算机网络；现代义是复合词的比喻延伸，不是古英语单词原义。

glossEn: study and treatment of the nervous system
derivation: neur（神经）+ o（连接元音）+ logy（学科）→ neurology
example: The neurology clinic sees many patients with migraine.

glossZh: 好的；友好的；令人愉快的

ety.from: 古法语 nice（愚蠢的、软弱的），源自拉丁 nescius（无知的，ne- 不 + scire 知道）
ety.note: 本义“无知、愚蠢”，中古英语后依次变为“羞怯、挑剔、精细、令人愉快”。现代“好”义与拉丁词根的“知/不知”已无共时形态联系，只能算词源关系。

glossEn: in a pleasant or satisfactory way
etymology: nice（古法语 nice < 拉丁 nescius 无知的）+ -ly
derivation: nice（令人愉快的）+ ly（副词后缀）→ nicely
example: The two boards fit nicely together after sanding.

derivation: nice（令人愉快的）+ ness（名词后缀）→ niceness
example: Her niceness made the long shift easier.

glossEn: the belief that nothing has real value or meaning
derivation: nihil（无）+ -ism（主义）→ 一切皆无的主张
example: The novel's ending drifts toward nihilism.

ety.from: nitre（硝石）+ -gen（产生）
ety.note: 18 世纪末科学拉丁语术语，因存在于硝石中得名。

example: The noise kept us awake.
derivation: noise（噪声） → 噪音
noise（噪声）+ less（没有……的）→ noiseless
example: A noiseless fan keeps the enclosure cool.

derivation: noise（噪声）+ y（形容词后缀）；去 e 加 -y → noisy
example: The gearbox grew noisy after the third run.

glossEn: existing in name only; very small in amount
derivation: nomin（名字）+ al（形容词后缀）→ nominal
example: The fee was nominal, so the lab paid at once.

glossEn: propose someone for a post or award
etymology: 拉丁 nominare（命名、提名）< nomen（名字）
derivation: nomin（名字）+ ate（动词后缀）→ nominate 把名字报上去
example: The board will nominate two candidates for the chair.

glossEn: not giving a single predictable result

etymology: non-（非）+ fiction < 拉丁 fingere（塑造）的分词词干 fictus
derivation: non（非）+ fict（塑造）+ ion（名词后缀）→ nonfiction
example: Her nonfiction account of the flood sold well.

derivation: non（非）+ line（线）+ ar（形容词后缀）→ nonlinear
example: The sensor response is nonlinear near saturation.

etymology: 拉丁 noxius < noxa「伤害」< nocere（伤害）
derivation: nox（伤害）+ -ious → 有害的
example: The plant releases noxious fumes when burnt.

glossEn: to make legally void or ineffective
etymology: 晚期拉丁 nullificare < nullus「无」+ facere（做）
derivation: null（无）+ -ify（使…）→ 使归于无
example: The court nullified the contract.

glossEn: the state of being legally void; nothingness
etymology: 中世纪拉丁 nullitas < nullus「无」
derivation: null（无）+ -ity（性质）→ 无效的状态
example: The lawyer argued for the nullity of the marriage.

glossEn: something thrown in the way, hence a thing perceived
the ability to judge without personal bias
derivation: ob（朝向）+ ject（投）+ ivity（名词后缀）→ objectivity 把判断投向对象而非自己
example: Peer review is meant to protect objectivity.

etymology: 拉丁 obnoxiosus < ob-（向）+ noxa（伤害），词义由「易受伤害」转为「惹人厌」
derivation: ob（向）+ nox（伤害）+ -ious → 一碰就伤人 → 讨厌的
example: His obnoxious jokes emptied the room.

glossEn: watch carefully; also, obey a rule
etymology: 拉丁 observare < ob-（朝向）+ servare（守护、留意）
derivation: ob（朝向）+ serve（守护）→ observe 守着看 → 观察，引申为遵守
example: Technicians observe the arc through a filtered window.
The format is obsolescent but legal.
etymology: 拉丁 obsolescere「渐渐不用」< solere 习惯于
derivation: ob（对着；反对；朝向） + sol（习惯于） + esc（表开始（起始后缀）） + ent（形容词/名词后缀：具有……性质的） → 逐渐过时的

etymology: 拉丁 obstaculum < ob-（对着）+ stare（站）+ -culum（工具、事物）
derivation: ob（对着）+ st（站，stare 的词干）+ acle（名词后缀：事物）→ obstacle 挡在面前的东西
example: Cost remains the main obstacle to a wider rollout.

glossEn: to block or get in the way of
etymology: 拉丁 obstruere < ob-（对着）+ struere（堆叠）
example: A fallen beam obstructed the service corridor.
derivation: ob（对着） + struct（建造） → obstruct

example: The obstruction was cleared within an hour.
derivation: ob（对着） + struct（建造） + ion（名词后缀） → obstruction
ob（对着） + struct（建造） + ive（形容词后缀） → obstructive
example: The scan showed an obstructive lesion in the airway.

etymology: 拉丁 obvius < ob viam（在路上）
derivation: ob（朝向）+ vi（道路，via 的变体）+ ous（形容词后缀）→ obvious 就在路上，一眼看见
example: The crack was obvious under the inspection lamp.

glossEn: close off or block a passage
etymology: 拉丁 occludere < ob-（对着）+ claudere（关）
derivation: oc（ob- 在 c 前的同化）+ clude（关，claudere）→ occlude
example: A clot can occlude the artery within minutes.

glossEn: the state of being blocked from view

etymology: ob-（向）+ currere「跑」→ 跑到跟前，发生；与 cura「关心」无关
derivation: oc（ob- 在 c 前的同化）+ cur（跑，currere；英语拼写中 rr 简作 r）→ occur 跑到面前 → 发生
注意：此处 cur 取“跑”义（currere），与 cura“关心”同形异源
example: Errors occur when the battery drops below ten percent.
note: currere「跑」，非 cura「关心」

derivation: octo（八） + pus（脚） → 章鱼（仿拉丁复数）

example: Zoologists once wrote octopodes.

derivation: octo（八） + pus（脚） → 章鱼（希腊式复数）

example: The octopus hid in the rocks.
derivation: octo（八） + pus（脚） → 章鱼

example: Two octopuses shared the tank.
note: 屈折形式
derivation: octo（八） + pus（脚） → 章鱼（英语化复数）

glossEn: relating to the eye or to sight
derivation: ocul（眼）+ -ar → 眼的
example: The infection causes ocular pain and redness.

etymology: 希腊 hodos（道路）+ metron（测量）
derivation: od（道路、行程）+ o（连接元音）+ meter（测量仪）→ odometer
example: The odometer showed forty kilometres after the loop.

glossEn: substance added to give a smell
derivation: odor（气味）+ ant（名词后缀：物）→ odorant
example: A trace odorant makes small leaks easy to smell.

etymology: 拉丁 odorifer < odor（气味）+ ferre（携带）
derivation: odori（气味）+ fer（携带）+ -ous（形容词后缀）
example: The odoriferous resin was burned as incense.

glossEn: the Theban hero of Greek myth
example: Oedipus solved the riddle of the Sphinx.
note: 希腊专名 Oidipous，不作词素切分

glossEn: to present for acceptance; a proposal
etymology: 古英语 offrian < 拉丁 offerre < ob-（朝向）+ ferre（带）
example: She offered to review the draft before submission.
derivation: ob-→of-（朝向）+ fer（带）→ 带到面前
→ 呈上、提供

glossEn: something presented as a gift or sacrifice
etymology: 古英语 offrung，offer 的名词形式
derivation: offer（献上）+ -ing（名词后缀）
example: The offering was placed on the altar before dawn.
She often walks to work.
note: 古英语 oft 加 -en 的副词，t 常不发音，整词处理

glossEn: rule by a small group of people
derivation: olig（少）+ arch（统治）+ -y → 少数人统治
example: The country slid from oligarchy into civil war.

glossEn: a market controlled by a few sellers
derivation: olig（少）+ o + poly（卖）→ 少数卖家把持市场
example: Three airlines form an oligopoly on that route.

etymology: 拉丁 omnis「全部」+ potens「有力量的」
derivation: omn（全）+ i + pot（能力）+ -ent → 无所不能的
example: The old king was described as almost omnipotent.

etymology: 拉丁 omnis「全部」+ vorare「吞食」
derivation: omn（全）+ i + vor（吃）+ -ous → 什么都吃的
example: Rats are omnivorous and adapt to almost any diet.
The opulent lobby glittered with gold.
etymology: 拉丁 opulentus < ops 财富
derivation: opul（财富） + ent（形容词/名词后缀：具有……性质的） → 富裕的；豪华的
orth（正、直）+ odont（牙）+ -ist → 把牙弄直的人
example: The orthodontist fitted her with braces.

glossEn: the conventional spelling system of a language
etymology: 希腊 orthos「正确的」+ graphein「写」
derivation: orth（正确）+ o + graph（写）+ -y → 正确写法
example: English orthography preserves many older pronunciations.

glossEn: to turn into bone; to harden
example: Rules ossify over time.
derivation: oss（骨） + ify（动词后缀：使成为） → 骨化；僵化

example: The ossuary holds the bones of monks.
derivation: oss（骨） + uary（……的场所（名）） → 藏骨堂

glossEn: in a different case; in other respects
etymology: 古英语 oþre wisan（以别的方式）
derivation: other（其他的）+ wise（副词后缀：在……方面/以……方式）→ otherwise
example: Log the offset, otherwise the next run will drift.

glossEn: located or used outside a building
derivation: out（向外）+ door（门）→ outdoor
example: The outdoor test ran from noon until dusk.

derivation: out（超过）+ number（数目）→ outnumber
example: Cheap units outnumber the calibrated ones in the field.

etymology: out-（超过）+ perform（古法语 parfournir 完成、执行）
derivation: out（超过）+ perform（执行、表现）→ outperform
example: The new model outperforms the old one on noisy data.

derivation: ov（卵）+ -ary（场所）→ 存卵之处
example: The scan showed a small cyst on the left ovary.

glossEn: judge something as larger than it is
etymology: over- + estimate < 拉丁 aestimare（估价）
derivation: over（过度）+ estim（估价）+ ate（动词后缀）→ overestimate
example: Do not overestimate the gain from a single trial.

glossEn: costs of running a business; above the head
etymology: over-（在上）+ head，18 世纪商业用语
derivation: over（在上）+ head（头）→ overhead 头顶之上 → 不直接产出的一般开支
example: Cloud overhead rose once the dataset doubled.

derivation: over（过度）+ work（工作）→ overwork
example: Do not overwork the pump during the first hour.

etymology: 拉丁 ovum「卵」+ 希腊 -oeidēs「像…的」
derivation: ov（卵）+ -oid（像…的）→ 卵形的
example: The vessel has an ovoid body and a narrow neck.

ety.from: 法语 oxygène，由希腊 oxys（尖锐、酸）+ -gène（产生）构成

example: The two states signed a pact.

derivation: pact（固定；约定） → 协定

glossEn: measurable factor that defines a system
etymology: 希腊 para（旁）+ metron（测量）；现代义经 17 世纪数学拉丁传入
derivation: para（旁、辅助）+ meter（测量）→ parameter 辅助量度 → 参数
example: Each parameter is logged together with its unit.
Patience is needed with young children.
etymology: 拉丁 patientia < pati 忍受
derivation: pat（感受、承受） + i（连接元音（空词缀）） + ence（名词后缀：状态、性质） → 耐心

ety.from: Portable Document Format 的首字母缩写

example: The telescope sits on a concrete pedestal.

etymology: 拉丁 pedester（步行的）< pedes（脚）

example: Traffic congestion is a perennial complaint in the city.

glossEn: outer boundary of an area, or its length

derivation: peri（环绕）+ meter（测量）→ perimeter 绕着量一圈
example: A fence runs along the perimeter of the site.

glossEn: length of time; one full cycle

etymology: 拉丁 persistere < per-（贯穿）+ sistere（站住）

example: The error persists even after a full reset.

etymology: 拉丁 petitio < petere「寻求、请求」

glossEn: the giving of money or help for human welfare

example: Her philanthropy paid for three rural schools.

glossEn: relating to or suffering from a phobia
derivation: phob（恐惧）+ -ic → 恐惧的
example: The reaction was more phobic than rational.

ety.from: telephone 的截短形式

etymology: 希腊 phōnētikos（与声音有关的）< phōnein（说话）< phōnē（声音）
derivation: phon（声音）+ etic（希腊形容词/学科后缀 -ētikos）+ s（学科名词）→ phonetics
example: Phonetics explains why the two vowels merge here.

ety.from: photograph 的截短形式
ety.note: 口语截去 -graph，只保留希腊词根 photo-（光）。

glossEn: semiconductor device that turns light into current
etymology: photo-（光）+ diode < 希腊 di-（穿过）+ hodos（道路）
derivation: photo（光）+ di（穿过）+ ode（道路，hodos）→ photodiode 让电流单向往光里走
example: The photodiode output tracks the laser pulse closely.

etymology: photo-（光、摄影）+ 希腊 gramma（记录）+ metron（测量）
derivation: photo（摄影）+ gram（记录）+ metry（测量术）→ photogrammetry
example: Photogrammetry rebuilt the facade from forty overlapping images.

ety.from: photo-（光）+ -graph（写、记录）
ety.note: 19 世纪光学与化学结合后造出的科学术语，用“用光写字”命名；不是古英语遗存。

glossEn: science of matter, force and energy
etymology: 拉丁 physica < 希腊 physika < physis（自然）< phyein（生长）

The picture hangs above the desk.

pixel（像素）+ ated（形容词后缀：具有……的）→ pixelated

glossEn: smallest units of a digital image (plural)
etymology: pixel 的复数；pixel 为 1960 年代 picture + element 的混成词
derivation: pixel（像素）+ s（复数后缀）→ pixels
example: The camera delivers twelve million pixels per frame.

glossEn: to make less angry; to appease

derivation: plac（使高兴）+ -ate（动词后缀）→ 使平息、安抚

ety.from: 拉丁 platea（宽阔的街道），源自希腊 plateia（宽），经古法语 place 进入英语

glossZh: 板状的（指鲨鱼等鱼的盾鳞）

example: The plough turned the wet soil.

example: Pneumonia kept the operator off work for a week.

ety.from: iPod + broadcast 的混成词

glossEn: treatment of foot and ankle disorders
etymology: 希腊 pous / podos（脚）+ iatreia（治疗）

example: Podiatry solved the gait problem the sensors missed.

glossEn: the practice of having more than one spouse
derivation: poly（多）+ gam（婚配）+ -y → 多配偶
example: The novel describes a family shaped by polygamy.

glossEn: a closed plane figure with many straight sides

example: The software fills any closed polygon with colour.

glossEn: music in which several voices sound together
derivation: poly（多）+ phon（声）+ -y → 多声部

student who continues after a first degree

glossEn: following the modern movement in art and thought
derivation: post（之后）+ modern（现代的）→ postmodern
example: The essay reads the archive in a postmodern way.

glossEn: note added after a letter's signature

derivation: post（之后）+ script（写）→ postscript

etymology: power（古法语 poeir < 拉丁 posse 能够）+ -ful

glossEn: concerned with doing rather than theory

She took a pragmatic approach to the budget.

derivation: pragmat（行为；事务） + ic（形容词后缀：……的、……性质的） → 务实的

glossEn: to base something on a stated fact; to assert

example: The argument is predicated on a false assumption.

glossEn: to like better; to put forward
etymology: 拉丁 praeferre < prae-（在前）+ ferre（带）→ 放在前面

→ 更喜爱；正式提出

prefer（置于前）+ -ent + -ial（形容词后缀）
example: Preferential tariffs apply to the least developed countries.

example: Pressure inside the tank rose faster than expected.

glossEn: advance showing before the public release

example: The preview build crashed on the second launch.
No prior experience is required.
derivation: pri（在前；第一） + or（名词后缀：施动者（拉丁来源）） → 先前的；优先的

example: She is proficient with both the mill and the lathe.

etymology: 希腊 programma < pro（在前）+ graphein（写）

example: The program stops if a checksum fails.

etymology: 拉丁 progressus < pro-（向前）+ gradi（走）

glossEn: something thrown forward, hence a plan

example: The trauma left a deep psychic wound.

derivation: quadr（四、方）+ -at- + -ic → 与平方有关的

glossEn: remember; ask for something to be returned

example: The solvent is volatile, so seal the jar.
